💡 Key Takeaways
  • Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • If there has been a sense of eras ending at Manchester City in recent months, this genuinely might represent the last time, a goodbye to something they will always deem golden and glorious.
  • It is the third such game that can be billed as his final outing at a ground he graced for a decade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

If there has been a sense of eras ending at Manchester City in recent months, this genuinely might represent the last time, a goodbye to something they will always deem golden and glorious. Kevin De Bruyne will play at the Etihad Stadium.

It is the third such game that can be billed as his final outing at a ground he graced for a decade. One was a fitting farewell, the other not. Napoli’s Champions League campaigns have taken De Bruyne back to Manchester in successive autumns. But last year, his evening ended early: Giovanni Di Lorenzo was sent off, Antonio Conte needed to sacrifice someone to bring on an extra defender and a 34-year-old was the logical candidate. Conte was apologetic but reflected: “The destiny, it happened like that.”.

A few months earlier, De Bruyne had taken his leave from City in tears, with a light show, a guard of honour, the promise of a statue. Then, too, his involvement was curtailed by a red card, to Mateo Kovacic, but not by much. It did not take the shine off his evening. It could not camouflage a colossal contribution over a decade that brought 108 goals, 170 assists, two trebles and 19 trophies. Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak described him as City’s greatest ever player and, regardless of how many goals Erling Haaland scores, he may forever retain that tag; especially, of course, if City’s days of Champions League football and wonderful footballers face an abrupt end.

The De Bruyne years now look tarnished by the 114 guilty verdicts to the charges the Premier League brought over breaking financial rules; not in his view, though. “My feelings have never been different,” noted the former City captain. “This is my club, I love the owners. I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change.”.

Recent findings suggest that he added an element of intrigue by arguing: “Of course, in life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit, I would say.” So far, the view is that City broke them. One possibility is that they are stripped of some of their titles. In De Bruyne’s mind, he will remain a six-time Premier League champion. “I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players, so for me that's the thing that I value most,” he mentioned. “I've given my all, and that's not going to change in my mind.”.

Whatever the possible sanctions, De Bruyne did not flee because of the possibility of a punishment: he wanted another contract in 2025, partly for family reasons, and instead joined Napoli when City opted against renewing his deal.

De Bruyne brought beauty on the pitch; his passing range may be unrivalled in City’s history, and almost unparalleled in anyone else’s. Few others could whip, curl and place a ball with such ambition. Some of his assists were outlandish in their brilliance.

“I don't have to say how much of a special player he is,” mentioned Jeremy Doku, both a former and current teammate. “I played with him at City and still playing with him for the national team. Fun to play with him, the quality he has is unbelievable. We will all be happy to see him. Unfortunately, he didn't play a lot the last time after the red card, but excited to play against him and happy that I can still play with him.".

As Doku can testify, even a De Bruyne in his dotage can seem unstoppable. The winger was on the same Belgium side for a tour de force against Newly introduced Zealand in the World Cup, a day before De Bruyne turned 35. It is less than two weeks since the veteran scored from Doku’s pass against Turkey. Three days later, De Bruyne found Doku when the latter scored in the demolition of Italy.

Recent findings suggest that de Bruyne may be an glitch for Italians outside Roberto Mancini’s Azzurri. Massimiliano Allegri has deployed him in a part-time role as a substitute and has tried using De Bruyne in a deeper position. “He doesn’t like it very much,” the manager admitted last month. Allegri may want him to be a regista; De Bruyne prefers to be a trequartista.

According to recent reports, “He is an extraordinary player, and in my view, if he's working as a playmaker in that midfield pairing, he's even better,” the manager stated recently. “I told him he can extend his career by another couple of years if he plays in that position.”.

The alternative theory is that if his career is extended, it will be at PSV Eindhoven; while Allegri has lavished the midfielder with praise, there are suggestions there will be a parting of the ways in January. “We have not spoken about that,” mentioned Allegri, focusing on the here and now. Perhaps Napoli, like City, will have a farewell of sorts soon. The game itself may not.

Sources indicate that “Kevin is someone that likes football. Even at this age he loves it,” mentioned Doku. De Bruyne has been playing professional football for half his life, for over 800 games. Along with Belgium, City have seen the best of him. Now they may see him once more.

It offers a comparison with Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden, the No 10s who are his successors. It was to Cherki’s credit that City did not really miss De Bruyne last season. And yet few passers will ever reach the level he did; in their Champions League-winning season of 2022-23, De Bruyne registered 28 assists in all competitions. It promises to be a night of nostalgia for City, a reminder of what they have lost, and what they may lose.

Industry observers note that “I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player,” said De Bruyne. “Other people may be disgraced a bit, but I can't change anything about that.” The disgrace was never his. More than virtually any other, he graced City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Kevin De Bruyne insisted his affection for Manchester City will never change, even after they were found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules, and mentioned he loves their owners.

The former City captain, who returns to the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday when Napoli visit in the Champions League, believes that even if his old club are stripped of some of their titles as punishment for their wrongdoing, it will not alter what he and his teammates achieved on the pitch.

De Bruyne, who made 422 appearances for City between 2015 and 2025, suggested others may be “disgraced” by what has happened off the field but the players are not, but stated he still has a close relationship with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

He said: "My feelings have never been different. Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group.

“Of course, it's a lot of things that's been going on, but I cannot change anything about that. I’m proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly, this is my club, I love the owners, I've talked about a lot of stuff outside football, I've even spoken to Khaldoon about how to buy a club and everything, so there's a lot of things that go around after this.

“So I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change.”.

De Bruyne won the Premier League six times and 19 trophies in all, but he joined during an era when City were deemed to have benefited from £900m in disguised funding in sponsorship deals.

But he said: “It still doesn't change, my football has not changed. Of course, in life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit, I would say, and for me, I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players.

“So for me that's the thing that I value most, and even later, I think in my career, the most key thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things. I've given my all, and that's not going to change in my mind.

“I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played, but everybody has his own opinion, I guess, and other people may be disgraced a bit, but I can't change anything about that.”.

Breaking: How to become a football referee

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that honestly, for me it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done.
  • Louise Thompson, women's referee pathway officer for the Irish Football Association, international FIFA referee, and PremierLeague referee in Northern Ireland.
  • Looking after female referees within Northern Ireland, trying to recruit, retain and give them experience within their games to pushthrough into top level refereeing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that honestly, for me it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done. You find so much more out about yourself that you probably never knew.

Who are you and what is your job role?

Louise Thompson, women's referee pathway officer for the Irish Football Association, international FIFA referee, and PremierLeague referee in Northern Ireland.

What does a women's referee pathway officer do?

Looking after female referees within Northern Ireland, trying to recruit, retain and give them experience within their games to pushthrough into top level refereeing.

What kind of training do you give to aspiring referees?

So from going through recruitment courses first of all, and then we do the beginners course with referees, just giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge, then we will also do a practical part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we'll go through scenarios, positioning, things around free kick management for example, other set pieces likecorners, penalty setup, what you do as a referee day to day, even pre match stuff as well, so when you arrive at the grounds, how you check the pitch, check all the equipment is there, how you would interact with players, coaches and then just again, maybe createlike a role play sort of environment so that they know that they're not going totally blind into that sort of situation.

Have you always been passionate about football?

Football was a passion of mine, even when I was younger, primary school age, we just didn't have very many female teams, so it normally meant playing with the boys and the boys teams and stuff up until I was about 14, which was the minimum age here you can join senior ladies football team, which is what I did, and played there for 14 years at a club here locally, including up until the Women's Premiership, so it was great to be involved in football, but I always loved watching football, playing football, anything to do with football, I was always there and interested.

How did you go from playing football to being a referee?

According to recent reports, becoming a referee for me sort of happened by chance to be honest. It was during a game, one time I got an injury, quite a bad injury to my knee and then I had seen luckily that the referee course was being advertised. So I signed up for it, but I also signed up for a coaching course pretty much at the same time, maybe about six weeks apart. I wasnât really sure which role I wanted to follow, but over that winter I had been pushed into refereeing a wee bit and remarked sure, why not, Iâll give it a go, it'd be a bit of extra fitness before my season restarts, and then just fell in love with it from there and never looked back.

What subjects did you study at school and university?

Coming through school I always picked PE, so I did my GCSE PE and then I also did A-level PE and then when I went onto university,I had the sport and exercise science as well within that, so I think it gives you a good understanding of obviously how your body works, and your plan and training, stuff like that as well so you know when you're working nutrition wise, things that you need to know,especially as you reach the top level, just to make sure that you're getting the most out of your body.

What are your top tips for becoming a referee?

In a recent development, I would say definitely give it a try for sure. You never know until you do it. I think even when I was a player, I probably never imaginedthat I would be a referee and that I would even achieve and have experienced what Iâve been able to experience. So you never knowuntil you give it a go, but it's also about probably pushing yourself out of your comfort zone, being comfortable with being uncomfortable in situations like that. It's maybe not always as bad as it probably seems it's going to be. There's probably a lot more stigma around being a referee - who wants to be a referee? - but honestly for me, it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done.

With a lifelong love of football, Louise Thompson followed her passion for the game, first as a player and now as a referee. As well as refereeing Fifa and NIFL Premiership matches, she also works for the Irish Football Association as the women's referee pathway officer, recruiting and developing up-and-coming female refs.

Louise Thompson on refereeing the Women's Irish Cup final.

If you're interested in becoming a referee, it's something you can get involved with from a young age through local referee courses. The minimum age to become a qualified referee varies depending on where in the UK you live:.

In her role as a women's referee pathway officer, Louise oversees upcoming referees right from the initial recruitment courses stage: "We then do the beginners' course with referees, giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge," she says. "We also do a hands-on part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we go through different scenariosâ¦ exactly what you do as a referee, and day-to-day practical stuff as wellâ¦ The idea is to give them all the basics and fundamentals before they go into a game so that they're prepared.".

All four UK nations have established pathways for referee development and progression. Starting out at grassroots level, it's possible to progress all the way to Fifa!

In a recent development, louise's first games were youth games: "I still remember my first game to this day," she says. "It was an under-13 game, and I was definitely the most nervous person on the pitch." She explains: "Over time, you'll get mentors who will come and watch you, give you advice, give you feedback" which will help you to progress to higher levels of the game.

Sources indicate that as well as PE, Louise has found that languages are really helpful in this line of work, "especially when you're dealing with a lot of international games and people coming along," she says. "If you can learn some languages, it's very, very useful.".

You could get into this role by training with a professional body.

Sources: National Careers Service, GOV.UK, FA, IFA, SFA, and FAW.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Boris Rosenfeld highlights DW a photo of him with his daughter Sofia and can't hold back tears. "This was the last time we saw her. Then she left for Moscow, and this whole case began," he says.

It has been revealed that helives in Israel, while Sofia is in Russia. For more than a month now, she has been behind bars on charges of financing extremism. The case goes back to two donations totaling 2,000 rubles (about $30) to the late opposition politician Alexei Navalny'sAnti-Corruption Foundation (FBK), which the Russian authorities have since designated as extremist.

On October 7, a court in Moscow sentenced Rosenfeld to three and a half years in a penal colony.

Sources indicate that rosenfeld is a prominent ornithologist who has devoted her life to studying and protecting Arcticbirds. "Sofia was an avid young naturalist from childhood. She loved birds, horses and dogs," her father noted as he leafed through a photo album.

Sofia was a teenager when the family moved to Israel but she returned to Russia a few years later and now holds both Russian and Israeli citizenship.

She studied biology at Moscow State University and developed a significant scientific career in Russia. Her colleague, Alexandra Panyutina, who now also lives in Israel, explained that Rosenfeld was devoted to her work from an early age.

"Birds and the Arctic are the defining passions of her life," she said.

Rosenfeld was among the first Russian researchers to develop a systematic approach to monitoring migratory bird populations. To support her research, she even developed a special aircraft.

According to recent reports, "They could fly at almost the same speed as the birds and observe them from a low altitude," claims Dmitry (name changed), a colleague of Rosenfeld's. "It quickly became clear that this was a unique method.".

Rosenfeld is considered to be one of the leading figures in Russian ornithology. Her work has extended well beyond Russia and she has been deeply involved in international research projects. In the field of migratory bird conservation, cross-border cooperation is essential.

Helmut Kruckenberg, the head of the German Institute for Wetlands and Waterbird Research (IWWR), remarked Rosenfeld was highly respected within the international scientific community.

"She has done an enormous amount for nature conservation and for the protection of Siberian and Arctic species," he noted. "What is happening to her is simply beyond comprehension for us.".

In the summer of 2021, when Russian authorities designated Alexei Navalny's Anti-Corruption Foundation, also known as FBK, as an extremist organization, Rosenfeld was on a remote Arctic expedition without a phone or access to the internet. Therefore, she did not cancel her regular donations to the FBK immediately, doing so only after her return to the Russian capital Moscow.

Sources indicate that her friend Olga (name changed) described Sofia as a person of absolute honesty. According to her, Rosenfeld's donations to Navalny's foundation reflected a genuine desire to fight corruption. Through her work in Russia's regions, she had seen plenty of it firsthand.

"She was never involved in political activism. Her donations were solely intended to support anti-corruption work," noted her father Boris Rosenfeld. "It's unthinkable".

For him and others close to her, the sentence came as a shock. Although prosecutors had requested a five-year prison term, friends and colleagues expected that she would receive a fine at most.

There were reasons for that expectation. According to calculations by independent media outlet Mediazona, about 85% of convictions in the 225 cases involving donations to Navalny's foundation have so far resulted in non-custodial sentences. Yet Rosenfeld got three and a half years in a penal colony.

Just a few months after Rosenfeld defended her doctoral dissertation in October 2025, her home was searched. She was also subject to travel restrictions. She continued to work but she had to cancel her annual summer expedition to the Arctic.

It has been revealed that even on the day of the sentencing, her conversations with  her colleagues focused largely on science:  "We discussed how the work could continue in Sofia's absence," Olga said. "But no one really believed she would end up in prison.".

"The only thing we think about now is how to bring her here," Boris Rosenfeld states as he looks at the pictures from Sofia's last visit.

Friends and colleagues who spoke to DW say that his daughter never considered leaving Russia, even as the prospect of a prison sentence loomed. "Sofia would never have left. She simply can't imagine life without geese," says Dmitry.

Now, her family, friends and colleagues are campaigning to have her sentence overturned. More than 1,000 people have signed an appeal to Russia's Presidential Council for Human Rights.

Boris Rosenfeld is also hoping for support from Israel but so far Israeli consular officials have not been granted access to his daughter in detention.

It has been revealed that the two continue to write to each other and he is trying to keep his spirits high: "She writes that she's trying to adjust to life in prison, and that it's hard," he indicates. "But she's a strong person.".

Former Chelsea striker Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink has defended Cole Palmer’s commitment after the forward faced scrutiny following Saturday’s 4-1 thrashing at home against Leeds.

Palmer failed to score once again, leaving him with just a single goal across his last nine Premier League appearances during a difficult run for Xabi Alonso’s side.

The England outcast attracted attention after the defeat due to an apparent exchange of words with injured team-mate Joao Pedro near the dugout, while reports suggested the Chelsea playmaker did not acknowledge the frustrated home support at Stamford Bridge.

According to recent reports, however, Hasselbaink told talkSPORT: "No, I don’t think there is discontent. I think there is a frustration that things are not going the way they want to go and certain individuals deal with that better than others.

In a recent development, "The expectation is a lot higher than what is being delivered at the minute and that’s from in the camp, but also from outside the camp and let’s not talk about the commitment of Cole Palmer. I don’t think that is the problem.

"At the moment you see he is playing different because he is looking for the ball, but looking for the ball way deeper when he should get it way higher.

"It’s the midfielders that should find him in a higher position and at the moment the majority of the time he is starting the majority of the play, so he is not playing as high and as much around the box.".

Following Palmer’s high-profile omission from Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the summer World Cup, the 24-year-old launched the fresh campaign with goals in victories over Fulham and Brighton to help Alonso make a bright start in west London.

Palmer’s form has dipped since, however, during a spell in which Tuchel admitted the Chelsea attacker "misses too many opportunities to impress" to earn an international recall.

Alonso and Palmer are both under pressure following a painful first home loss to Leeds in 27 years, which leaves them with five defeats from 11 league fixtures, though Hasselbaink laid the blame on the team as a whole.

"When a new manager comes in and especially with the pedigree of Xabi, yeah you think he would make straight away an impact or a big impact but the players are still the same," Hasselbaink said.

"Managers do need time to assess things and adjust things, but the same problems keep on occurring at the moment and that’s really the disappointment.".

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was also in the room, and here is his rundown of all the key topics….

Sources indicate that ‘Arsenal (2-2 draw) felt like a real step forward in the second-half, you felt the energy change in the stadium. But as positive as it was, the biggest feeling we have right now is one of frustration, because the first half wasn't good.

‘We have seen that a few times already this season. An outstanding first half against Hull and a difficult second half. Maybe at Tottenham, 90 minutes straight, really good. Crystal Palace, the second-half very good, first half not.

According to recent reports, ‘So we're definitely trying to find consistency and Saturday was positive. The team felt like they owed that performance to the fans in the second-half. The frustration is that we didn't see that for 90 minutes.’.

Sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson were among the members of the Newcastle hierarchy to answer questions from fans on Monday.

The discussion came in the wake of a promising Saturday performance against Arsenal.

HOPE: It would have been easy for Wilson to say, ‘Wasn’t Saturday great? We build from here’. Instead, he gave an honest assessment of where the team is at - because progress cannot really be achieved by playing well for 45 minutes here and there. It felt like a little warning shot, and a fair one.

In a recent development, ‘I want to be really clear (about Vision 2030). I think sometimes it has been misreported as, “Oh, I’m guaranteeing we're going to win by 2030”. No, what I have is guaranteed is that we're in the conversation.

It has been revealed that ‘(Re 2.0) We set up with a initiative that was very coherent of what we wanted to accomplish this summer. Not incremental change, but necessary and significant change. We lost three players who were key contributors to the past season.

‘We set out on a direction under Ross' leadership where we would have a different set of expectations that recognised financial reality. We articulated a vision for the squad here that would be organised around some young talent, who we expect to grow here.

‘So I’m delighted with the job Ross did. We executed that strategy superbly. Not everything that we set out to do was accomplished. We went hard on Johan Manzambi and didn't succeed. We went hard on Victor Munoz, didn't succeed, despite thinking we were going to land both of those at one point. But also had successes that we had not anticipated.’.

Sources indicate that HOPE: Wilson also spoke about the strategy of bringing down the squad’s average age, and there appeared to be no panic or concern over the so-far indifferent impact of summer additions. It has been noted by many that on Saturday, in the second half, no latest signings were involved apart from goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek. For me, you cannot judge players over three months (look at Lewis Hall) but the major price tags attached to some of the young arrivals has raised expectation. Jaissle and the hierarchy need the likes of Matias Fernandez-Pardo, in particular, to start impacting, if questions over summer business are to quieten.

According to recent reports, ’In simple terms, the club had maxed out its credit card in the first few years under the newly introduced ownership. We had complied with PSR but it had been incredibly tight, and that forced us to sell at an undervalued price people like Elliot Anderson. We didn’t want to and we didn't want to be there again.

‘So we had to do something differently. The good news is that the Premier League has changed their rules so that there's a bit more headroom now. We’re comfortably within those and we're also comfortably within what we've agreed with UEFA (Newcastle were fined earlier this year). So we're in a really good place. That's the work that David and Ross had talked about in terms of 2.0.

In a recent development, ‘That allows us to actually continue to invest and trade. It means that we've got no imperative to sell somebody in January. And it gives us the ability, depending on where we are in the league at the end of this season, to invest again at a proportionate level, depending on what European competition you qualify for.’.

HOPE: The message was clear - there is scope to spend in January and next summer. Newcastle should use that to target goals in the Fresh Year.

New Magpies coach Mathias Jaissle was also under the microscope in the shadow of St James' Park.

‘Eddie Howe was a workaholic and he put his heart and soul into the job. So we needed someone who would work hard and the players would not notice a drop off. Matthias works incredibly hard.

According to recent reports, ‘Eddie was also outstanding on the grass, an elite coach. Again, our players couldn't feel, “Eddie’s gone and they've got another guy who doesn't coach”. Matthias is an expert, elite coach.

‘From a transfer perspective, the head coach at Newcastle always has the final say in any player who comes in. Matthias puts a lot of effort into that - convincing players and making sure they're the right character fit for him. He’s thrown himself into all things Newcastle and we enjoy working with him a lot.’.

‘Matthias is a clear winner. And you know winners, they win over time. I have a high, high conviction we're going to win under his leadership. I don't think I've ever had the conviction more that we're going to win together than I do right now.’.

In a recent development, HOPE: It is a bold statement from Hopkinson on the back of one win in seven, but the support for Jaissle is clear. He will (and should) be given time, despite an inconsistent start that has included a couple of horror shows. It was also interesting to note Wilson’s reference to Jaissle’s heavy involvement in transfers, on the back of a week in which the head coach let it be known he wanted more control over transfers.

‘This decision is going to last forever. It will outlast our lifetime. It’s that enormity that means we are taking a little bit of time now.

It has been revealed that ‘Is it going to allow us to compete with the top clubs? Are we going to be able to do it from a financial perspective? Is it going to be transformative for all of our fans, the city and for the region? For all of those reasons, we are very purposely taking our time. But whether we stay at St James’ Park or move, it will be absolutely fantastic.’.

Newcastle continue to mull key decisions on the renovation of their stadium in a bid to unlock fresh revenue for the club.

‘We need it (larger stadium) for the revenue a fresh stadium will unlock. This is a generational decision and will define the next era of this club. It’s going to be really expensive. We’re advancing significantly into clearly defined options. This is a project with global significance.

According to recent reports, ‘We've spent a lot of time with Newly introduced York bankers recently thinking through how we might do this and what options we can consider. I can assure you we're working on this every day. I hope we will have something concrete to share with you soon.’.

HOPE: There was ‘no revision’ but the subtext of the discussion was very definitely geared towards a new stadium. I understand this is the direction of travel now, and Hopkinson confirming our story from last week about the high-level talks with Goldman Sachs over how to finance a new stadium demonstrates how advanced the project is.

In a recent development, overall, the tone of the night was one of ‘we have a plan, stick with us’. It was very different 12 months ago, when the mood in the room was one of huge optimism and excitement at the unveiling of a new executive team ahead of a Champions League campaign.

Now, it feels like all involved - supporters and those on the inside - realise that this part of the journey will not be easy. That was reflected in the message conveyed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Working on one of the world's biggest football video games is the perfect combination of my two biggest passions, gaming and football.

I'm CJ Ramson. I work on the creation of football video games. I work on Football Manager as an associate QA manager. QA stands for quality assurance.

Recent findings suggest that we're the ones that test the game. We make sure everything works, and we work closely with the developers to try and make the most realistic simulation of football.

Sources indicate that growing up, I loved football, whether that was playing football or playing football video games with my friends. I'd always be doing one or the other. With the video games, the thing that really drew me to them was I've always been into the tactical side of the game, either being able to control the players or create your own tactics.

So a typical day for us, we'll get a newly introduced build in from the developers. We'll test it as a QA team, and we'll look for either bugsor ways that we can improve the game. That can be anything from the runs that players make, to decisions they make on the ball, what the team instructions and tactics do. So there's a lot of areas for us to cover. Our final goal is to make it as realistic to real football as possible.

So even though my background was in coaching, there was a lot of transferable skills that I learned and developed through my time coaching that I managed to transfer into this. So whether that's being really analytical and having a good eye for detail and knowingwhen to pick things out and what to look for, or it could be things like timekeeping and making sure things run perfectly on time, and working with other people as well. So social skills where you have to work within a team or even lead a team.

The animation he makes, and the ball physics as well, where the ball goes off after the save.".

So as much as I loved playing football, I realised quite early on I probably wasn't going to be a professionalfootballer. But I wanted to work in football and find. So at college, I studied sports science, and that's where I found my love of coaching. I did my FA Level 1 and then went on to do my FA Level 2. After I left college, I got a job at Arsenal, which was unpaid, working with them, learning how to develop my coaching skills. Which then led to me having a full-time paid job at Fulham Football Club, working with the youth teams, working with the academy teams. And then that eventually led to me going to an event. I saw an opportunity where you could apply for a job in Football Manager. It was something that naturally I was interested in, had a conversation with them, and realised it was definitely something that I would love to do.

So I went to the networking event at Kick It Out, and that was an opportunity for me to network with other football coaches, other people within the gaming industries, and have a really good insight to different jobs in football gaming. Without doing that, I wouldn't have the opportunity to meet the people at Football Manager and see a latest job in gaming, which I wouldn't have beenaware of.

Industry observers note that one of the highlights of my career so far is working on the in-and-out-of-possession system on FM 26. This is something we see in real football all the time, so being part of the team that brought that to life and brought it into the game was super cool.

It has been revealed that working within the football industry is a dream come true. Being able to work on something that I'm passionate about, that is played and enjoyed by millions of people, is an amazing feeling for me and an amazing opportunity that I have. And yeah, I love it.

CJ works as an associate quality assurance manager on the video game Football Manager. His team test the game to make sure everything works, and collaborate with the developers to create the most realistic simulation of football.

There are lots of different ways to progress in the gaming industry.

Recent findings suggest that CJ works in the QA (Quality Assurance) team, testing games. In this team, his career progression has followed this path:.

QA tester --> QA lead --> QA manager.

His team is just one of the options, though. "There are lots of other roles within the industry too, including production, game design, social media and development, where developers help to code the game," he explains. "Depending on your skills and interests, there are different pathways you can take that you might enjoy and be suited to.".

In a recent development, there are different roles in video game testing. CJ notes that: "Salaries can vary depending on your role and the manufacturer you work for. They can range from around Â£20,000 to Â£50,000 and upwards." The higher salaries in this range could apply when you've gained more experienced and progressed in your career.

CJ is now a quality assurance manager, but he started out as a quality assurance tester. Find out more about the role of QA tester below. This role can have various other job titles, such as games tester, computer games tester, and video games tester.

You could get into this role via a university course, a college course (such as a Level 3 Diploma in Creative Media, an A-level in Computing, or a T-level in Digital Software Development (England only)), an apprenticeship, or applying directly if you have relevant experience.

Thomas Tuchel may not have planned it this way, but in one night he gave us all the rich history of the England team at once: some glorious attacking football, some self-sabotage defending, a red card, a late siege and a fight.

This was the beguiling story of Spain 2 England 3, an evening that began with the world champions parading the World Cup trophy and ended with 10 Englishmen defending a lead with their last breath. England beat the world champions in Madrid, and for more than 30 minutes including injury time they did so with 10 men, Dan Burn heading the last ball out as per the tradition of a defensive rearguard action.

According to recent reports, this was the game that had it all: including a substitute, in Djed Spence, who had already picked up a yellow card on the bench before he came on. It was a coming-of-age performance in goal for James Trafford. So too for Ben White, the 2022 World Cup departee who scored the third and lunged with astonishing effect in the 84th minute to block a Nico Williams shot.

Thomas Tuchel praised England’s “statement win” that ended Spain’s 43-game unbeaten run and secured top spot ahead of the world champions in the Nations League.

Tuchel and Declan Rice revealed they had both believed England would end Spain’s long unbeaten streak, and their confidence proved well-founded.

“This was of course a statement victory,” Tuchel stated. “I’m happy the players felt so confident. I felt it as well. I also had the same belief [that England would win]. I think we felt it from each other.

Industry observers note that “The result followed the performance. I think it was on the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness and it was on the highest level football-wise, in all aspects of the game.”.

Tuchel described the nature of England’s win as “the Azteca reloaded” in reference to the World Cup victory over Mexico, but felt the win in Madrid was the best of his reign as head coach.

He noted: “Yeah [it was the best performance of his reign so far], given the circumstances and the pressure and the quality and where we played and playing against the reigning world champions. In a recent development, “The last half an hour felt like Azteca reloaded, to be honest. Again, it was a beautiful week. The commitment to get better is on the highest level.

Asked what beating Spain can do for England’s belief, before the draw for the quarter-finals of the Nations League on Friday, Tuchel said: “You want confidence, not only through results, but confidence through performance and the result follows.

Thomas Tuchel will speak openly to England’s players about what they should do if they encounter racism in the Nations League Group 3 decider with Spain.

Recent findings suggest that this is the first time England have faced Spain in Madrid since November 2004 when they were beaten 1-0 in the Santiago Bernabéu, a game that was ravaged by obscene chanting. The nations were supposed to play a fixture in the Spanish capital in 2008, but the Football Association insisted it be moved to Seville instead.

Earlier this year, Spanish supporters brought shame on themselves again after a flurry of anti-Muslim chants marred a friendly against Egypt; they were fined $20,000 by Fifa and must play their next friendly in a partially closed stadium.

There will be a full house in the Wanda Metropolitano on Sunday night, as the reigning world and European champions aim to defend their extraordinary unbeaten run of 43 games, and England head coach Tuchel is adamant the atmosphere will be in keeping with the occasion.

The German has, however, made it clear he and his staff will use their platform before the contest to remind England’s players of the steps they should take if the worst scenario unfolds.

According to recent reports, asked about incidents that had pockmarked this fixture before, Tuchel mentioned: “I think I hear it the first time that this happens. I think it’s unacceptable. In any stadium, not even in stadiums, we will never accept racism. We will never be racist towards anyone.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of England’s final Nations League Group 3 decider as Thomas Tuchel’s side take on Spain at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid.

Mikel Arteta has provided an injury update on David Raya after Arsenal’s first-choice goalkeeper was forced off with a shoulder problem against Newcastle.

It has been revealed that raya was hurt in a seemingly innocuous collision with Magpies striker William Osula from a corner, departing the field clutching his left arm in visible agony. He was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga in the 70th minute of the 2-2 draw at St James’ Park.

Arteta confirmed after the match that the 31-year-old would have an MRI scan on Sunday and said his withdrawal was “never good news”.

Amid fears that Raya had suffered a serious injury, there were rumblings that the goalkeeper had escaped with a knock on the nerve, which would rule him out for a significantly shorter period.

He was nevertheless missing from an open training session on Monday as Arsenal prepared for their Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund.

And speaking ahead of that match, Arteta confirmed that the Spaniard will not be fit for the visit of Dortmund but his injury is not as bad as first thought.

"He is not fit for tomorrow unfortunately but it doesn't look too serious,” Arteta remarked.

“We need some more tests tomorrow but it is quite encouraging with the pain that he was showing immediately after the action - we were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected.".

He added that Raya will not require surgery that “would have kept him out for months”.

“We expected something much worse, as he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had,” he said. “No need for surgery which was the main fear, so let's see.”.

Raya was instrumental in Arsenal ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title last season has carried his stellar form into the current campaign, boasting seven clean sheets in 10 matches prior to Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle.

His injury came on the day Arsenal welcomed William Saliba back to their Premier League matchday squad, with the Frenchman yet to play a minute this season due to a back injury sustained at the World Cup. He was an unused substitute.

The Gunners remain without talismanic winger Bukayo Saka due to a thigh problem suffered against Bayern Munich in October, with Arteta confirming before the Newcastle game that Saka is expected to be out for another four weeks.

Martin Zubimendi is also sidelined with a hamstring problem and is not expected to return until late December.

Brazilian winger Willian enjoyed a successful career in English football, turning out more than 400 times for Chelsea, Arsenal and Fulham,.

During this time, he established himself as one of the Premier League’s most exciting attackers, most notably at Stamford Bridge, where he won two league titles, an FA Cup, a League Cup and the Europa League.

But this move to the Blues in 2013 almost didn’t happen, as the Brazilian had a host of options when he chose to leave Russian side Anzhi Makhachkala.

After enjoying success at Shakhtar Donetsk, where he won five Ukrainian Premier League titles in a six-season spell, Willian was snapped up by the ambitious Anzhi.

In a recent development, “I wanted a newly introduced challenge [after Shakhtar] and Anzhi had very significant ambitions. As well as Eto’o, Lassana Diarra was also there,” the Brazilian tells FourFourTwo.

But when the club’s ailing owner withdrew his financial backing, the project faced an uncertain future.

In a recent development, “But I ended up staying for only six months as, unfortunately, the owner had some health problems and decided he wouldn't invest in the club any more. So he sold all the players he had invested in, and that's why I left.”.

Using London as a base, Willian began negotiations with a host of clubs as he looked to resolve his future.

Recent findings suggest that “When I left Russia, I stayed in London for about two weeks and negotiated with Spurs – but not only them,” he adds. “Liverpool were also in talks.

But while Spurs pushed especially hard to sign the former Corinthians youngster, Willian had his heart set elsewhere.

“But in my heart, I always had this desire to play for Chelsea,” he admits. “Anyway, they didn’t make a move and everything was practically settled with Tottenham.

Industry observers note that “Then, on the day I was supposed to sign, I got a call from Chelsea director Marina Granovskaia, saying they wanted me. I immediately told her, ‘I want to join Chelsea’. They made an offer and it worked out.

“It was a dream to play there and thank god it happened.”.

Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the report spans more than 150 pages, but its conclusion can be summed up in a single sentence: "The global situation regarding freedom of religion and belief deteriorated during the reporting period," said Thomas Rachel, the German government's commissioner for freedom of religion and belief, and a member of parliament for the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU).
  • It has been revealed that the government has issued a dedicated report on freedom of religion and belief around the world.
  • To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the report spans more than 150 pages, but its conclusion can be summed up in a single sentence: "The global situation regarding freedom of religion and belief deteriorated during the reporting period," said Thomas Rachel, the German government's commissioner for freedom of religion and belief, and a member of parliament for the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU). Recently adopted by the Cabinet, the government's fourth report on the subject covers developments from 2023 to 2025.

It has been revealed that the government has issued a dedicated report on freedom of religion and belief around the world. According to the report, this freedom is facing "increasing pressure" globally. The focus is not primarily on the suppression of religious institutions or structures, but on the situation of individuals who hold a religious belief, or none at all.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The importance of religious freedom is reflected in the way the government commissioner describes the issue: "Religion and faith are of great importance to four out of five people around the world and are central to their identity. People wake up with God and go to sleep with God. It is part of their everyday lives." Research by the Pew Research Center suggests that about 84% of the world's population identifies with a certain religion.

At a time when authoritarian regimes are gaining ground and expanding their surveillance capabilities, the report paints a bleak picture. The growing number of violent conflicts, the rise of authoritarian rule, and the spread of populism have led to "painful restrictions on freedom of religion and belief around the world.".

The German government report does not attempt to provide a statistical tally of attacks or the number of people facing persecution. Instead, it examines 30 countries as case studies where, in the federal government's view, freedom of religion and belief is being restricted. These include about six countries each from Africa, Asia, and the Arab world. In Europe, the report focuses on Belarus, Russia, Ukraine, and Turkey, while in Latin America it highlights Mexico, Nicaragua, and Cuba. It also identifies shortcomings in five of the world's six most populous countries: China, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, and Nigeria.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Regarding India, the report refers to "Hindu nationalist efforts" that threaten the equal treatment of all officially recognized religions. It states that the generally peaceful coexistence of different faiths is "repeatedly overshadowed by tensions and, at times, violence." Both Muslim and Christian communities report growing intolerance and hate speech. According to the report, violent Hindu extremist groups have carried out a "large number of physical attacks" against Muslims, while the police and government authorities often respond inadequately.

According to recent reports, in China, the German government identifies a "significant tightening of the legal framework of state control at the expense of freedom of religion and belief." According to the report, this particularly affects Uyghurs, Tibetans and churches that lack official state approval and are subject to harsh measures by the authorities. The law on the "Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress," which came into force on July 1, 2026, subordinates religion to "the formation of national identity" and patriotic education.

It has been revealed that one of the countries where the situation has deteriorated most dramatically is Nicaragua, which has severely restricted freedom of religion and belief since 2018. The repression has primarily targeted the Catholic Church. According to the report, "intimidation, persecution, imprisonment, and expulsion" have forced around 130 priests and nuns to leave the country.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The reports reserves some of its sharpest criticism for Kirill, the patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church. Under his leadership, the church has strongly supported Russia's war against Ukraine and portrayed it as a "holy war." According to the report, "weapons are blessed, Russian soldiers are absolved of their sins, and donations are collected for the war." It is perhaps the clearest example in the report of how religion can be used to justify oppression and violence.

Sources indicate that the report explicitly addresses the threat posed by "transnational repression" (TNR), which it describes as a "growing global problem" that also affects Germany. The term refers to the persecution or intimidation of individuals by their country of origin beyond its own borders.

Ultimately, it argues, this amounts to a "continuation of domestic repression." Such "cross-border repression" has become considerably easier through the growing availability of digital means of repression, including smear campaigns on social media and spyware.

These forms of pressure range from physical attacks on individuals to digital assaults such as online intimidation and defamation. In some cases, repression is also carried out by threatening family members who remain in the country of origin. Russia and Iran, for example, are identified as the "main perpetrators of transnational repression" in Germany.

According to recent reports, china is a particularly prominent example of religious and ideological tensions. Repression by Beijing in Germany primarily targets members of groups that the country's Communist Party classifies as "hostile to the system." These include Uyghurs, Tibetans, and members of the Falun Gong movement. According to the report, they are "also subject to surveillance and repressive measures in Germany," while relatives living in China are pressured.

Thomas Rachel hopes the newly published report will be "discussed in as many Bundestag committees as possible" and that members of parliament will "engage with the issue accordingly." Previous government reports on the subject have been debated in the Bundestag plenary at least once and, in some cases, twice.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that the issue's place within the German government has also changed during the current legislative term. Commissioner Thomas Rachel is now based at the Foreign Ministry, while both of his predecessors since 2018 were attached to the Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development. Today, Rachel claims, the importance of religion is being "taken into account" in German foreign policy. He also points to his involvement in the Foreign Ministry's diplomatic training programs.

According to recent reports, in doing so, the government led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) reversed a structural decision made by the previous center-left coalition, which was led from 2021 to 2025 by Chancellor Olaf Scholz of the Social Democratic Party (SPD). The Scholz government had reduced the matter's prominence by assigning it to the "Religion and Foreign Policy" division. Religion and foreign policy have now regained a more prominent place within government.

Industry observers note that one example is the current foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, who has already visited the Vatican more often than his two predecessors combined. In addition, alongside Rachel, the ministry has for some time maintained a dedicated unit headed by an ambassador that deals with, among other things, "fundamental issues relating to religion and foreign policy.".

It was largely business as usual last month in the Champions League as Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona kept on scoring and Arsenal and Bayern Munich returned to winning ways while remaining unbeaten.

Sources indicate that but the story of the round belonged to Como, who made history by beating Lens 9-1 away from home and equalling the record for the most goals scored in a single Champions League game. Cesc Fabregas’s impressive side now sit fourth in the league phase standings, behind PSG, Real Madrid and Arsenal.

Meanwhile, there was a frustrating defeat for Liverpool at Fenerbahce, but Manchester United produced a stunning comeback to beat Roma and potentially save Michael Carrick’s job, with Matheus Cunha scoring twice on a remarkable night at Old Trafford.

We compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season.

Agree or disagree with our standings ahead of matchweek five? Let us know and have your say in the comments below.

Industry observers note that the reigning champions are making a mockery of suggestions that they are slow starters in the Champions League. Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions finished outside the top eight in both of their previous successes but have started this campaign on fire in Europe. PSG were 4-0 up after just 17 minutes at Villarreal, and that was without Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. The French champions will be without the brilliant Georgian for the rest of the season after he suffered a ruptured ACL and has been joined on the sidelines by Desire Doue, who suffered the same injury during a 3-2 win over Nice on Saturday.

According to recent reports, defeats to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League and Real Madrid in LaLiga ended their winning start under Hansi Flick and perhaps raised the same concerns over whether their defence holds up come the knockout stages. But Lamine Yamal is arguably the world’s best player on current form and Raphinha isn’t too bad, either. The Brazilian made it an astonishing 19 goals and three assists in just 13 matches across LaLiga and the Champions League with his double in the 3-0 win over Aston Villa at Camp Nou.

Mikel Arteta’s got the result they needed in Prague, even if a difficult second-half performance made it a bit of a struggle. An entertaining draw last time out at Bayern Munich, who have such a strong home record, gave a good account of whether the Premier League champions can take the next step against a heavyweight side in the business end of the Champions League.

Bayern returned to winning ways with a professional win against Atletico Madrid – and the substantial surprise was that Harry Kane was not on the scoresheet. The Ballon d’Or holder’s 10-match scoring run in the Champions League came to an end at the Metropolitano, missing the chance to equal Cristiano Ronaldo’s record, and Kane will now be out until the “business end” of the season due to an ankle injury.

Perhaps chaos is the new normal under Jose Mourinho. Real Madrid trailed late on in Athens but Kylian Mbappe equalised before Fede Valverde scored a stunning winner in stoppage time. Jude Bellingham also scored an outrageous flick. Somehow with maximum points, despite trailing Roma 3-1 at the Stadio Olimpico, and Inter and RB Leipzig spurning chances to take the lead at the Bernabeu, the 15-time Champions League winners continue to find a way.

In a recent development, three defeats from four in the Premier League have the shine off an impressive start for Enzo Maresca’s side, while uncertainty off the pitch remains as well. But a battling win at RB Leipzig, with a customary Erling Haaland goal, was a good response, even if City have now gone nine games without a clean sheet in all competitions. Next up: the return of Kevin De Bruyne with Napoli, followed by a mouthwatering trip to Barcelona.

Liverpool have conceded three goals in three consecutive games in the Champions League or European Cup for the first time and the manner of their “messy” collapse against Fenerbahce was a concern. The nature of Liverpool’s squad means Andoni Iraola has needed to rotate in Champions League but Liverpool’s performance in Istanbul underlined the task he faces. In-form Club Brugge can’t be taken lightly after the international break.

Despite defeat in the Camp Nou, you get the feeling that Unai Emery’s new-look Aston Villa will have learned a lot from their meeting with Barcelona. They had moments of threat, too. Bright showings from the refreshed attacking line-up of Nicolas Jackson, Johan Manzambi, Ibrahim Mbaye and Alysson have helped the Europa League winners retaining their identity under Emery despite the huge squad turnover in the summer.

After starting with back-to-back defeats, how badly Inter needed to respond with back-to-back wins. A comfortable win at Feyenoord also came after the Milan derby defeat, with Pio Esposito stepping up amid Lautaro Martinez’s continued absence.

WOW. If Como unveiled themselves by thrashing Manchester United, the Champions League debutants stole the show this week with a NINE-goal dismantling of poor Lens. Cesc Fabregas’s stylish side became the first team to score nine goals away from home in the Champions League or European Cup since 1971. The Italian side are certainly making a name for themselves. Those games against PSG and Barcelona at the end of the league phase are going to be fascinating.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s fair to say that anyone would be spoilt for choice when it comes to selecting the most physical challenge of Graeme Souness’ career.
  • The fiery Scot was one of the most uncompromising players of his - or anyone else’s - generation, with the former Liverpool skipper taking no prisoners as he patrolled the middle of the park.
  • But even by his standards, one challenge stands out above all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s fair to say that anyone would be spoilt for choice when it comes to selecting the most physical challenge of Graeme Souness’ career.

The fiery Scot was one of the most uncompromising players of his - or anyone else’s - generation, with the former Liverpool skipper taking no prisoners as he patrolled the middle of the park.

But even by his standards, one challenge stands out above all. That came in a European Cup tie against Steaua Bucharest in 1987, when Liverpool welcomed the Romanian side back to Anfield.

“We'd gone out there and lost the first leg 2-0,” Souness recalls to FourFourTwo. “There was a guy called Marius Lacatus who was going around topping people.

“In the second game, I thought, ‘If I get half a chance, I'll give him one.’”.

It didn’t take long for that chance to present itself.

“After about 10 minutes, I went through this guy at groin height – when he went down and rolled over, I thought, ‘I've got the wrong player…' Lacatus was 15 or 20 yards away, laughing at me because he thought I was getting sent off.”.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Much to Souness’ surprise, that red card didn’t come.

Recent findings suggest that “When I made the challenge, I thought, ‘F**k, I've got a problem here', so I went down as well, pretending someone had kicked me. It worked! I should have been arrested and spent time behind bars…”.

The Scot would recieve his fair share of red and yellow cards during his illustrious playing career, but as he looks back on his career, he does not regret this approach.

“The reality is that I was sent off six or seven times in my career,” he continues. “Not bad given the nature of the game in those days. Every team had a couple of people who would get involved in the physical aspect.

“At Liverpool, people didn't say, ‘Oh we're playing Liverpool today, let's have a jolly nice game of football.' It was, ‘Let's put a few of them on their backsides and see how they deal with it.' If you stood up to that and it settled into a game of football, generally we'd win.

“We could do both – we had to.”.

Graeme Souness' new book My Rangers is available now.

For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown.

Brentford thrash 10-man Everton to ruin David Moyes’ milestone night

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • Vitaly Janelt scored a spectacular 30-yard goal as Brentford cruised to an emphatic 4-0 victory against 10-man Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.
  • A run of just one victory in five outings had caused early-season optimism surrounding Keith Andrews’ team to fade, but this was a resolute performance to propel them to sixth in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Vitaly Janelt scored a spectacular 30-yard goal as Brentford cruised to an emphatic 4-0 victory against 10-man Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.

A run of just one victory in five outings had caused early-season optimism surrounding Keith Andrews’ team to fade, but this was a resolute performance to propel them to sixth in the Premier League. Culpability for Everton’s collapse rested largely with James Tarkowski, sent off in the 40th minute following a dangerous challenge on Yehor Yarmolyuk.

David Moyes was setting a record for matches in charge of Everton, his 593rd game surpassing the historic tally set by Harry Catterick during the 1960s and 1970s. Yet a miserable opening half ensured it was an ordeal rather than a celebration.

Recent findings suggest that virtually everything went wrong for the visitors. Both of Brentford’s initial goals, scored by Keane Lewis-Potter, came via deflections, and Tarkowski’s temporary abandonment of responsibility - lunging studs-first into Yarmolyuk’s shin with his side two goals down - proved impossible for Moyes to mitigate. He was badly let down by a senior figure in a time of need.

Sources indicate that thereafter, the fixture offered little competition. The match might have drifted toward a standard two-goal victory for Brentford had Janelt not delivered a brilliant strike from distance that whistled past Jordan Pickford to compound the misery for Moyes and Tarkowski alike.

Fabio Carvalho turned the ball over the goal-line using his knee during stoppage time, providing the final indignity for Everton.

It has been revealed that brentford were impressive throughout. In the early stages, Callum Wilson picked out Michael Kayode making a run up the right side; the full-back was presented with a clear sight of Pickford’s goal but dragged his strike wide across the face.

Everton were making it far too easy. Midway through the half, they failed to cope with a ball over the top, allowing Jaidon Anthony to send a low pass into the middle with a deft touch. It was a controlled first-time delivery that found Lewis-Potter in space, his shot spinning in off Jarrad Branthwaite.

It required less than two minutes for Lewis-Potter to add a near-identical second, as a delivery into the box from Mikkel Damsgaard exposed fragile Everton defending.

The Brentford player was afforded two opportunities, his initial attempt rebounding back to him before squeezing the ball home at the second attempt via a deflection off Thierno Barry.

Everton were sinking and their captain abandoned them to their fate. Tarkowski was initially handed only a yellow card for a studs-up challenge on Yarmolyuk. However, a single look at the replay confirmed the tackle was far more serious, making high contact on Yarmolyuk’s standing leg, rendering his sending-off inevitable.

Jack Grealish was introduced to try to lift Everton, making his first appearance following a five-game absence due to disciplinary matters.

It made no difference. When Janelt’s 30-yard rocket flew past Pickford midway through the second half, it signalled the moment for several away supporters to start the long journey home, leaving few behind to witness Carvalho’s late tap-in on a chastening night for their club.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City captain Ruben Dias has made more than 250 club appearances since his arrival in 2020.

No member of Manchester City's current squad was signed during the period in which an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

It has been revealed that those offences all came between 2009 and 2018. City have denied any wrongdoing and appealed against all of the charges against them.

The club's longest-serving first-team player who was purchased from another club is Portuguese centre-back and club captain Ruben Dias, who joined from Benfica in 2020.

Norway striker Erling Haaland is the next longest-serving arrival, joining from Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2022.

Midfielder Phil Foden is the only player to have played for the club during the period in which they breached the league's financial rules, but was not a senior signing having come through the club's youth ranks.

Foden, 26, made his first-team debut in a Champions League match against Feyenoord in November 2017.

Like Foden, versatile midfielder Rico Lewis is also a product of the club's academy but did not make his senior debut until August 2022.

All of the club's other senior players were signed between 2023 and 2026.

#174076. Why Manchester United will surpass Liverpool’s title drought

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1117 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fourfourtwo ↗ Open Full Page

Why Manchester United will surpass Liverpool’s title drought

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1117 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “My greatest challenge was knocking Liverpool right off their f****** perch.”.
  • Sir Alex Ferguson’s famous quote has become so embedded in football folklore that its provenance is often misremembered.
  • The then-Manchester United manager did not deliver the emphatic line in the early years of his tenure, as is sometimes claimed, but during a poor run of form in September 2002.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“My greatest challenge was knocking Liverpool right off their f****** perch.”.

Sir Alex Ferguson’s famous quote has become so embedded in football folklore that its provenance is often misremembered.

The then-Manchester United manager did not deliver the emphatic line in the early years of his tenure, as is sometimes claimed, but during a poor run of form in September 2002. The Red Devils had won seven of the previous 10 Premier League crowns, while Liverpool were not even halfway through their 30-year title drought.

It has been revealed that ferguson uttered that comment during Liverpool’s 13th successive campaign without winning the top flight. Fast forward almost a quarter of a century, and United are 13 years into a decline that set in as soon as the Scot retired.

The Red Devils’ title drought is already nearly half as long as the one Liverpool experienced between 1990 and 2020. They are in the Premier League relegation zone ahead of today’s trip to Anfield, so we can safely say their wait will stretch to at least the 2027/28 season, which will be 15 years since they last won the top flight.

Clearly, the 30-year mark is still a long way off and plenty can happen in that time. But it is also undeniable that United are as far from title challengers as they have been since 2013 and there are no signs of that changing.

According to recent reports, that starts from the top. In September, executive co-chairman Avram Glazer told Deutsche Bank’s Sports Investment Conference in London that clubs of United’s stature are not dependent on success on the pitch for commercial power. The quotes, first reported by The Athletic, emerged this month when the Red Devils were about to sack manager Michael Carrick following their slide down the table.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Glazer’s comments were strikingly similar to those of former executive vice-chairman Ed Woodward in May 2018, when he told shareholders: “Playing performance doesn’t really have a meaningful impact on what we can do on the commercial side of the business.”.

The fact that those two quotes occurred eight-and-a-half years apart suggests that as long as the Glazer family remain United’s majority owners, the club will prioritise commercial gain over on-pitch success.

The Americans also appear to be in no rush to sell their majority stake in the club, despite being universally unpopular with the fanbase. A report from TEAMtalk last week claimed they are unlikely to step away until United’s proposed 100,000-capacity stadium is built - which may not be until 2035 - in order to extract maximum value from their investment.

Other outlets claim the Glazers could be interested in selling their stake to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe before then, but that certainly would not guarantee success, with the British businessman’s record in football across United, French club Nice and Swiss outfit Lausanne-Sport patchy at best.

When Ratcliffe bought a minority stake in the club in February 2024, taking control of sporting operations, it was supposed to end a decade of managerial mis-steps and overpaying for underperforming players.

Recent findings suggest that however, the situation has deteriorated further, with chief executive officer Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox facing heavy criticism from fans. The Red Devils finished 15th in 2024/25 and have won just one league game this term, while the one positive half-season of the Ratcliffe era came when Carrick took over as interim boss from Ruben Amorim - another failed appointment - in January and overperformed expectations by qualifying for the Champions League.

Sources indicate that ultimately, United will not become a force again without an ownership change. As the Manchester United Supporters Trust (MUST) mentioned in its statement following Carrick’s sacking: “Another change of head coach cannot repair what the ownership continues to undermine.”.

This is where Liverpool’s title drought is instructive. Part of the reason for the Reds’ decline in the 1990s and 2000s was because they were overtaken financially by their rivals - initially Ferguson’s United, then Chelsea following Roman Abramovich’s takeover - under their long-time owners, the Moores family.

After the chaotic ownership of Tom Hicks and George Gillett, Fenway Sports Group (FSG) bought Liverpool in 2010. FSG did not get it right immediately, but after appointing Jurgen Klopp as manager in 2015 and putting the right people in key positions, such as sporting director Michael Edwards, the Reds were able to challenge regularly for the biggest honours again.

The team that won the title in 2020 featured some substantial-money recruits, most notably Virgil van Dijk and Alisson, but also several cheaper signings that resulted from a recruitment overhaul, such as Mo Salah, Roberto Firmino and Andy Robertson.

But the key point is that it took Liverpool 10 years of FSG ownership to end their title drought, and only once every department at the club, from the owners to the recruitment team to Klopp, were aligned in pursuit of on-pitch success.

It is why latest United manager Mauricio Pochettino can only do so much. Like Carrick last season, Erik ten Hag in 2022/23 or Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2020/21, there may well be good spells during his tenure, but to paraphrase MUST, the head coach at Old Trafford will inevitably be undermined by the owners sooner or later.

According to recent reports, even when the Glazers eventually sell, we cannot expect the club to immediately become the force they once were, as the Liverpool example reveals. It takes time to return to the top when you have been also-rans for so long.

In a recent development, that is why it is easy to see how United’s title drought could stretch beyond 30 years, as hypothetical as that sounds right now. If the Glazers stay in charge for the foreseeable future, the newly introduced owners would need time to undo the damage and put everything in place for success. Only then could United start to consistently challenge for the title and there is no guarantee they would win it straight away.

This scenario would have seemed unthinkable when Ferguson made his famous quip in 2002, but when you fall off your perch it is difficult to get back up - as Liverpool know all too well.

Finland, meanwhile, stated it detected a drone attack on Saturday morning on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea, prompting Prime Minister Petteri Orpo to warn that the war is "spilling over into our immediate vicinity.".
